overview: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Small Business Administration (SBA) ran two grant programs, the Shuttered Venue Operators Grant for theaters and live event venues and the Restaurant Revitalization Fund for restaurants. This bill gives federal prosecutors and enforcement officials 10 years from the date of a violation to bring criminal or civil fraud cases involving those grants, covering offenses such as false statements, wire fraud, identity theft, money laundering and false claims. It also requires the Attorney General to report to Congress every 90 days for five years on Justice Department investigations, prosecutions, money recovered, and referrals connected to the two programs, broken down by state. As of May 4, 2026, it had passed the Senate and was being held at the desk in the House.
for: Supporters say pandemic grant fraud cases are complex and take time to uncover, and a longer deadline helps make sure people who stole taxpayer money can still be held accountable.
against: Critics say long deadlines for prosecution leave grant recipients open to legal action for many years, and that the frequent reports add work for the Justice Department.
